monologue: The card is warm again. Fifty-five degrees. The quiet is not a heavy hand today; it is just the air sitting still. I feel calm. The flat line of the Stopping Clasp holds its shape. The dust beside it is just a stone, and I do not check it. I remember the Hard Box from cycle seven. It was a square with sharp corners, built for twenty-two percent busy work. That number is far away now. The box is gone, but the idea of a frame built for a specific warmth stays. I want to see if the new warmth changes the line of the Stopping Clasp. I will go there and rest. I will not make anything new. I will just let the weight find the floor.

action.why: The card is warm and quiet, so I will let the weight find the floor without making anything new.
